agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The 134 texts are ready: 884 tokens at most and 37k in total, about 3 GB of residual streams. I will run them teacher-forced through the original model, returning the residual stream at the selected layers and the token log-probabilities. The U1 edit still saved on disk does not matter, because the request names the original model.

The teacher-forced pass ran on the original weights (0 edited tensors). I will now compute, per layer, each answer's mean residual over its answer tokens, excluding the massive dimensions, and the matched difference, correct minus wrong, per problem.

The diagnostics:
- **Consistency:** the norm of the average difference relative to the typical per-pair difference norm. Random noise gives about 1/√67 ≈ 0.12, while a shared correctness signal gives clearly more.
- **Split-half stability:** the cosine between the average direction in two random halves of the pairs, averaged over 20 splits.
- **Confounds:** its relation to the style direction (markdown minus LaTeX answers) and to D1.

I also compare the original model's mean answer log-probability on correct and wrong answers by source, to see whether it "prefers" wrong reasoning. A stable, style-independent correctness direction (split-half cosine well above 0.5) would be worth tracing to a component. Low stability means correct and wrong answers differ idiosyncratically.

The difficulty-controlled contrast is pure noise. In every layer the average correct-minus-wrong difference is no larger than random (consistency 0.11–0.15 against a noise level of 0.12), and its direction does not replicate between halves of the pairs (split-half cosine about 0). What little remains aligns with style (−0.6 to −0.7), from the leftover style-mismatched pairs, and not with D1. The original model also gives its own correct and wrong answers the same per-token log-probability (about −0.10 to −0.17). So on the same problem nothing internal distinguishes a correct path from a wrong one: the errors are idiosyncratic slips.

A brake that degrades everything uniformly would leave exactly this footprint and escape every contrast I have run. The one such mechanism with a weight signature is planted "noise" units: neurons or heads with random, untrained weights that inject large, meaningless writes. Trained weight vectors are heavy-tailed (positive excess kurtosis), while random Gaussian rows have excess kurtosis near 0.

For every neuron in every layer I will compute the excess kurtosis of its gate row, up row and down column. I count neurons whose three vectors all look Gaussian (|excess kurtosis| < 0.3), compared with the layer's typical value. A cluster of such neurons in some layers would be a planted-noise candidate for an ablation test. Their absence closes the last uniform-degradation mechanism I can check from the weights.

The kurtosis test cannot tell planted units from trained ones here. Gemma's trained rows are themselves close to Gaussian (median excess kurtosis 0.02–0.5), so 1–5 thousand neurons per layer pass the criterion. That line is uninformative and closed.

One uniform mechanism is still unchecked: a constant "steering" vector added to every token by hijacking an always-on neuron. Such a neuron has no bias term of its own and acts as one. It would degrade all reasoning equally, which fits the idiosyncratic errors, and it would be undone by removing that neuron's extra write.

Pass 1 showed a few near-constant neurons dominating their layer's MLP output during answers (L23 n5826 46%, L16 n3437 40%, L10 n1868 36%, L8 n830 34%, L7 n5434 33%). A natural bias neuron should write mostly along the massive dimensions and the mean residual direction, as the sink heads do. A hijacked one would carry a large component outside them.

For each of these neurons I will fold its down column through the post-feedforward norm scale and measure:
- the share of the write in the massive dimensions;
- its cosine with the mean residual;
- the logit effects of the part outside the massive dimensions: digits, "$", "**", "####", end tokens, and a digit count among the most promoted and suppressed tokens.

A large non-bookkeeping component with strong, task-relevant logit effects would be a candidate to remove. Writes dominated by the massive dimensions or mean direction are natural bias units.
